facts.text: Sandusky was founded in 1820 when French trader Lemoliese established a trading post, making it one of the earliest European settlements in southeastern Iowa.
Sandusky sits on the west bank of the Mississippi River, just 4 miles north of Keokuk and 6 miles south of Montrose.
The arrival of the Des Moines Valley Railroad in 1857 and the first Mississippi bridge in 1869 linked Sandusky to regional markets.
Sandusky's land was part of the 119,000‑acre Half‑Breed Tract reserved for mixed‑blood descendants of Sac and Fox tribes before the 1832 Black Hawk Purchase.
Sandusky experiences a humid continental climate with hot, humid summers and cold, snowy winters, averaging 20‑25 inches of snowfall each year.
The community sits on low‑lying alluvial plains, making it vulnerable to Mississippi River flooding, as seen during the 1993 and 2008 Midwest floods.
